If a video has no captions, a\n[Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper)-compatible ASR service transcribes it.\n\n## Quick start (self-hosted)\n\n```bash\ndocker run --rm \\\n  -e YTT_PUBLIC_URL=https://your-domain.example.com/ytt \\\n  -e YTT_PATH_PREFIX=/ytt/ \\\n  -e YTT_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS=your-oauth-subject \\\n  -e YTT_WHISPER_URL=http://your-whisper:8000 \\\n  -p 8080:8080 \\\n  ghcr.io/jedarden/ytt:0.1.0\n```\n\nThe server starts at `http://localhost:8080/ytt`. Returns inline text for short videos; paginated chunks + `next_cursor` for long videos. Auto-starts Whisper ASR if no captions exist. |\n| `get_transcript_job` | Poll a Whisper ASR job. When done, returns the transcript directly. |\n\nPass any YouTube URL form: `youtu.be/…`, `?v=`, `/shorts/`, `/live/`, bare 11-char ID — all normalize to the same cache entry.\n\n## Requirements and caveats\n\n| Requirement | Notes |\n|-------------|-------|\n| **Residential egress IP** | YouTube blocks datacenter IPs. Self-hosted on a home server or residential VPS works natively. For VPS/cloud, set `YTT_PROXY_URL` to a residential proxy (e.g. Webshare). |\n| **Whisper endpoint** | Required only for videos without captions. Point `YTT_WHISPER_URL` at any OpenAI-compatible ASR service (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`). Run [whisper-openai](https://github.com/stpb/whisper-openai) locally, or skip and accept `no_captions_asr_failed` for caption-less videos. |\n| **Single replica** | In-process state (LRU cache, single-flight, Whisper job registry). Scale-out requires a redesign. |\n| **Auth required** | OAuth 2.1 with a subject allowlist. Empty allowlist = deny all. |\n\n## Configuration\n\nAll config is environment-variable-based — no ardenone-specific values are\nbaked into the image.\n\n| Variable | Default | Description |\n|----------|---------|-------------|\n| `YTT_PUBLIC_URL` | `https://mcp.ardenone.com/ytt` | Public base URL — OAuth audience + emitted metadata derive from this. See [connector.md](docs/usage/connector.md) for how to discover your `sub`. |\n| `YTT_WHISPER_URL` | `http://whisper-openai.whisper-stt.svc.cluster.local:8000` | OpenAI-compatible ASR endpoint. |\n| `YTT_WHISPER_MODEL` | `Systran/faster-whisper-small` | Model name served by the Whisper endpoint. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_7ab3370469374fc6adad3243","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge\n2\t\n3\tbead-forge (`bf`) is a repo-local issue tracker built for multi-agent AI coding workflows. Each \"bead\" is a task (bug, feature, research item, etc.) stored as JSON entries in a JSONL file alongside your code. Agents claim beads, work on them, and close them — like a task queue where each worker is an LLM session.\n4\t\n5\tbead-forge is a drop-in replacement for [`beads_rust`](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`) — every `br` command works unchanged. On top of that it adds **atomic claiming** via SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, so 20 workers can claim work simultaneously without racing each other.\n6\t\n7\t```bash\n8\t# Drop-in: symlink br → bf\n9\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n10\t\n11\t# Claim the next available bead atomically (no race conditions)\n12\tbf claim --assignee worker-1 --format json\n13\t\n14\t# Split a large bead into children atomically\n15\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 --children '[{\"title\": \"Implement handler\"}, {\"title\": \"Write tests\"}]'\n16\t\n17\t# Show all commands, including br-compatible ones\n18\tbf --help\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\t## The Beads Ecosystem\n22\t\n23\tbead-forge is the third generation of a repo-local issue tracker lineage:\n24\t\n25\t**[beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (Steve Yegge, Python)**\n26\tThe original. A git-backed issue tracker designed as \"memory for coding agents.\" Each issue is a JSON object; every update appends to a JSONL log. SQLite is a read cache, not the source of truth. A DAG of `blocks/blocked_by` dependencies lets `bd ready` return the next actionable task. Designed for single-agent use — no concurrency story at all.\n27\t\n28\t**[beads_rust](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`, Jeffrey Emanuel, Rust)**\n29\tFast Rust port of beads. 10–100× faster than the Python original. Adds `sync --flush-only / --import-only`, a `doctor --repair` command, TOON output format (token-optimized for LLMs), and orphan handling. Maintains full JSONL and `.beads/` compatibility. Our codebase runs a fork of this with a rusqlite shim replacing the upstream FrankenSQLite backend ([upstream issue #171](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/issues/171)). Concurrency story is identical to `beads` — SQLite single-writer, no atomic claiming.\n30\t\n31\t**bead-forge (`bf`, this repo)**\n32\tSuperset of `br`. Preserves 100% of the JSONL format, `.beads/` directory layout, and CLI surface so existing scripts, NEEDLE workers, and CLAUDE.md instructions that reference `br` continue to work without changes. Adds atomic claiming, critical-path scoring, velocity tracking, and crash-safe batch operations — the features required for reliable multi-worker fleets.\n33\t\n34\t## Problem\n35\t\n36\t`br` claiming is a client-side read-then-write race:\n37\t\n38\t```\n39\tWorker A: br list → sees bead-123 (open, highest priority)\n40\tWorker B: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n41\tWorker C: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n42\t\n43\tWorker A: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → SUCCESS\n44\tWorker B: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n45\tWorker C: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tWith 11+ workers, 10 workers waste cycles on retries. Observed in production: 4 workers simultaneously claiming the same bead, pervasive phantom claims with 20-worker fleets.\n49\t\n50\tThe `br` busy_timeout prevents `database is busy` failures but doesn't prevent the thundering herd. The rusqlite shim fixed SQLite corruption but not contention.\n51\t\n52\t## Solution: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction\n53\t\n54\tbead-forge runs the entire read-score-pick-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:\n55\t\n56\t```sql\n57\tBEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n58\t  SELECT id, priority, critical_path_float\n59\t    FROM issues\n60\t   WHERE status = 'open'\n61\t     AND NOT EXISTS (\n62\t           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n63\t            WHERE d.blocks_id = issues.id\n64\t              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues b WHERE b.id = d.blocked_by_id AND b.status != 'closed')\n65\t         )\n66\t   ORDER BY priority ASC, critical_path_float DESC\n67\t   LIMIT 1;\n68\tUPDATE issues SET status = 'in_progress', assignee = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?;\n69\tCOMMIT;\n70\t```\n71\t\n72\tSQLite's write lock serializes the transaction. The second worker to arrive blocks for ~0.5–2 ms (microseconds of actual work) then picks the next available bead. No phantom claims. No server required — the database file itself is the coordination primitive.\n73\t\n74\t## Architecture\n75\t\n76\t```\n77\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n78\t│                        .beads/                              │\n79\t│  issues.jsonl   ← append-only audit log (source of truth)  │\n80\t│  beads.db       ← SQLite query cache + bf-only tables       │\n81\t│  config.yaml    ← workspace config (bf fields are additive) │\n82\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n83\t          ↑ read/write\n84\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n85\t│                     bf (bead-forge CLI)                      │\n86\t│                                                             │\n87\t│  Claiming  ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic, serialized)     │\n88\t│  Mitosis   ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic split)           │\n89\t│  Batch     ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic multi-op)        │\n90\t│                                                             │\n91\t│  Critical path ── DAG float via recursive CTE               │\n92\t│  Velocity      ── p50/p90 close times per model+type        │\n93\t│  Annotations   ── key/value on any bead                     │\n94\t│  Event log     ── operation history per bead                │\n95\t│  Secret scan   ── pre-commit hook (gitleaks rules)          │\n96\t│  Rotation      ── archive closed beads older than N days    │\n97\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n98\t```\n99\t\n100\t### bf-only SQLite tables\n101\t\n102\tThese tables are additive — `br` ignores them when operating on a migrated workspace, so `br` and `bf` can be used interchangeably on the same `.beads/` directory.\n103\t\n104\t| Table | Purpose |\n105\t|-------|---------|\n106\t| `bead_annotations` | Arbitrary key/value metadata per bead |\n107\t| `worker_sessions` | Active worker registry (name, model, started_at) |\n108\t| `velocity_stats` | p50/p90 close times per model + harness + issue_type |\n109\t| `critical_path_cache` | Pre-computed DAG float scores (invalidated on dep changes) |\n110\t| `operation_log` | Full event history per bead |\n111\t\n112\t### Data authority: SQLite vs JSONL\n113\t\n114\t**CRITICAL**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n115\t\n116\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n117\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n118\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n119\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n120\t\n121\t**Why the inversion**: Multi-worker fleets need atomic read-modify-write operations (`bf claim`, `bf mitosis`, `bf batch`). These execute inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions on SQLite. JSONL is append-only and cannot support atomic read-write cycles.\n122\t\n123\t**Implication**: Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist **only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n124\t\n125\t### Flush-before-repair rule\n126\t\n127\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. To protect against data loss:\n128\t\n129\t```bash\n130\t# ALWAYS flush first (or use --flush-first)\n131\tbf sync --flush-only\n132\tbf doctor --repair\n133\t\n134\t# OR use the safe flag\n135\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n136\t\n137\t# OR force (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n138\tbf doctor --repair --force\n139\t```\n140\t\n141\tIf unflushed beads exist and neither `--flush-first` nor `--force` is specified, `repair` refuses with an error listing the beads that would be lost.\n142\t\n143\t**Why this matters**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads were permanently lost.\n144\t\n145\t### Claim scoring\n146\t\n147\t`bf claim` selects the highest-priority ready bead using a composite score:\n148\t\n149\t1. **Priority** — P0 always beats P1, etc.\n150\t2. **Critical path float** — among equal-priority beads, pick the one on the longest blocking chain (finishing it unblocks the most downstream work)\n151\t3. **Velocity affinity** — optional: route beads to workers whose historical p50 close time for that `issue_type` is fastest\n152\t\n153\t### Compatibility with br\n154\t\n155\tbead-forge is a strict superset of `br`. bead-forge\n\nbead-forge (`bf`) is a repo-local issue tracker built for multi-agent AI coding workflows. Each \"bead\" is a task (bug, feature, research item, etc.) stored as JSON entries in a JSONL file alongside your code. Agents claim beads, work on them, and close them — like a task queue where each worker is an LLM session.\n\nbead-forge is a drop-in replacement for [`beads_rust`](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`) — every `br` command works unchanged. On top of that it adds **atomic claiming** via SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, so 20 workers can claim work simultaneously without racing each other.\n\n```bash\n# Drop-in: symlink br → bf\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n\n# Claim the next available bead atomically (no race conditions)\nbf claim --assignee worker-1 --format json\n\n# Split a large bead into children atomically\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 --children '[{\"title\": \"Implement handler\"}, {\"title\": \"Write tests\"}]'\n\n# Show all commands, including br-compatible ones\nbf --help\n```\n\n## The Beads Ecosystem\n\nbead-forge is the third generation of a repo-local issue tracker lineage:\n\n**[beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (Steve Yegge, Python)**\nThe original. A git-backed issue tracker designed as \"memory for coding agents.\" Each issue is a JSON object; every update appends to a JSONL log. SQLite is a read cache, not the source of truth. A DAG of `blocks/blocked_by` dependencies lets `bd ready` return the next actionable task. Designed for single-agent use — no concurrency story at all.\n\n**[beads_rust](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`, Jeffrey Emanuel, Rust)**\nFast Rust port of beads. 10–100× faster than the Python original. Adds `sync --flush-only / --import-only`, a `doctor --repair` command, TOON output format (token-optimized for LLMs), and orphan handling. Maintains full JSONL and `.beads/` compatibility. Our codebase runs a fork of this with a rusqlite shim replacing the upstream FrankenSQLite backend ([upstream issue #171](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/issues/171)). Concurrency story is identical to `beads` — SQLite single-writer, no atomic claiming.\n\n**bead-forge (`bf`, this repo)**\nSuperset of `br`. Preserves 100% of the JSONL format, `.beads/` directory layout, and CLI surface so existing scripts, NEEDLE workers, and CLAUDE.md instructions that reference `br` continue to work without changes. Adds atomic claiming, critical-path scoring, velocity tracking, and crash-safe batch operations — the features required for reliable multi-worker fleets.\n\n## Problem\n\n`br` claiming is a client-side read-then-write race:\n\n```\nWorker A: br list → sees bead-123 (open, highest priority)\nWorker B: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\nWorker C: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n\nWorker A: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → SUCCESS\nWorker B: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\nWorker C: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n```\n\nWith 11+ workers, 10 workers waste cycles on retries. Observed in production: 4 workers simultaneously claiming the same bead, pervasive phantom claims with 20-worker fleets.\n\nThe `br` busy_timeout prevents `database is busy` failures but doesn't prevent the thundering herd. The rusqlite shim fixed SQLite corruption but not contention.\n\n## Solution: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction\n\nbead-forge runs the entire read-score-pick-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:\n\n```sql\nBEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n  SELECT id, priority, critical_path_float\n    FROM issues\n   WHERE status = 'open'\n     AND NOT EXISTS (\n           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n            WHERE d.blocks_id = issues.id\n              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues b WHERE b.id = d.blocked_by_id AND b.status != 'closed')\n         )\n   ORDER BY priority ASC, critical_path_float DESC\n   LIMIT 1;\nUPDATE issues SET status = 'in_progress', assignee = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?;\nCOMMIT;\n```\n\nSQLite's write lock serializes the transaction. The second worker to arrive blocks for ~0.5–2 ms (microseconds of actual work) then picks the next available bead. No phantom claims. No server required — the database file itself is the coordination primitive.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        .beads/                              │\n│  issues.jsonl   ← append-only audit log (source of truth)  │\n│  beads.db       ← SQLite query cache + bf-only tables       │\n│  config.yaml    ← workspace config (bf fields are additive) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n          ↑ read/write\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     bf (bead-forge CLI)                      │\n│                                                             │\n│  Claiming  ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic, serialized)     │\n│  Mitosis   ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic split)           │\n│  Batch     ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic multi-op)        │\n│                                                             │\n│  Critical path ── DAG float via recursive CTE               │\n│  Velocity      ── p50/p90 close times per model+type        │\n│  Annotations   ── key/value on any bead                     │\n│  Event log     ── operation history per bead                │\n│  Secret scan   ── pre-commit hook (gitleaks rules)          │\n│  Rotation      ── archive closed beads older than N days    │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### bf-only SQLite tables\n\nThese tables are additive — `br` ignores them when operating on a migrated workspace, so `br` and `bf` can be used interchangeably on the same `.beads/` directory.\n\n| Table | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `bead_annotations` | Arbitrary key/value metadata per bead |\n| `worker_sessions` | Active worker registry (name, model, started_at) |\n| `velocity_stats` | p50/p90 close times per model + harness + issue_type |\n| `critical_path_cache` | Pre-computed DAG float scores (invalidated on dep changes) |\n| `operation_log` | Full event history per bead |\n\n### Data authority: SQLite vs JSONL\n\n**CRITICAL**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\n**Why the inversion**: Multi-worker fleets need atomic read-modify-write operations (`bf claim`, `bf mitosis`, `bf batch`). These execute inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions on SQLite. JSONL is append-only and cannot support atomic read-write cycles.\n\n**Implication**: Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist **only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n\n### Flush-before-repair rule\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. To protect against data loss:\n\n```bash\n# ALWAYS flush first (or use --flush-first)\nbf sync --flush-only\nbf doctor --repair\n\n# OR use the safe flag\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n\n# OR force (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\nbf doctor --repair --force\n```\n\nIf unflushed beads exist and neither `--flush-first` nor `--force` is specified, `repair` refuses with an error listing the beads that would be lost.\n\n**Why this matters**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads were permanently lost.\n\n### Claim scoring\n\n`bf claim` selects the highest-priority ready bead using a composite score:\n\n1. **Priority** — P0 always beats P1, etc.\n2. **Critical path float** — among equal-priority beads, pick the one on the longest blocking chain (finishing it unblocks the most downstream work)\n3. **Velocity affinity** — optional: route beads to workers whose historical p50 close time for that `issue_type` is fastest\n\n### Compatibility with br\n\nbead-forge is a strict superset of `br`. Every `br` command works identically:\n\n| Command | Behavior |\n|---------|----------|\n| `br create / list / show / update / close / reopen` | Identical output, identical JSONL entries |\n| `br ready` | Same DAG-based filtering; bf adds critical-path sort |\n| `br sync --flush-only / --import-only` | Same JSONL format |\n| `br doctor --repair` | Same repair logic; bf-only tables are not affected |\n| `br dep / br label / br search / br stats` | Identical |\n\nThe symlink `br → bf` is all that's needed on a migrated machine. Scripts that call `br` call `bf` automatically.\n\n**Forward-compatibility note**: `bf` adds a `content_hash` column to the `issues` table. If `br` is run directly on a migrated workspace, `br doctor` may emit a column-count mismatch warning. This is cosmetic — data is not affected and `br` reads/writes continue to work correctly.\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\n[NEEDLE](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE) is a fleet orchestrator that spawns LLM-powered workers (Claude Code, GLM variants) to process beads in parallel. bead-forge was built specifically to support NEEDLE fleets at scale.\n\n### How workers claim beads\n\nNEEDLE's `pluck` strand calls `bf claim` instead of the old `br list` + `br update` two-step:\n\n```bash\n# Old (race condition with 11+ workers)\nBEAD=$(br list --format json | jq -r '.[0].id')\nbr update $BEAD --status in_progress --assignee $WORKER\n\n# New (atomic, no race)\nbf claim --assignee $WORKER --format json\n```\n\nA single `bf claim` call acquires the next available bead in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. Pluck strand: primary bead selection from the assigned workspace.\n//!\n//! Pluck handles >90% of all bead processing. It queries the bead store for\n//! unassigned, ready beads, filters by excluded labels, and sorts them in\n//! deterministic priority order: `(priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC)`.\n//!\n//! Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same candidate list.\n\nuse crate::bead_store::{BeadStore, Filters};\nuse crate::types::{Bead, StrandError, StrandResult};\n\n/// Default labels excluded from Pluck selection when not configured.\nconst DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS: &[&str] = &[\"deferred\", \"human\", \"blocked\", \"starvation-alert\"];\n\n/// The Pluck strand — primary work selection.\npub struct PluckStrand {\n    /// Labels to exclude from candidate selection.\n    exclude_labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Auto-split beads after this many consecutive failures (0 = disabled).\n    split_after_failures: u32,\n}\n\nimpl PluckStrand {\n    /// Create a new PluckStrand with the given exclude labels.\n    ///\n    /// If `exclude_labels` is empty, the default set (`deferred`, `human`,\n    /// `blocked`) is used.\n    pub fn new(exclude_labels: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        let labels = if exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (*s).to_string())\n                .collect()\n        } else {\n            exclude_labels\n        };\n        PluckStrand {\n            exclude_labels: labels,\n            split_after_failures: 3, // default threshold\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new PluckStrand with the given exclude labels and split threshold.\n    ///\n    /// If `exclude_labels` is empty, the default set (`deferred`, `human`,\n    /// `blocked`) is used.\n    pub fn with_split_threshold(exclude_labels: Vec<String>, split_after_failures: u32) -> Self {\n        let labels = if exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| (*s).to_string())\n                .collect()\n        } else {\n            exclude_labels\n        };\n        PluckStrand {\n            exclude_labels: labels,\n            split_after_failures,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Extract the failure count from a bead's labels.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. Returns the count if found,\n    /// or 0 if no failure-count label exists.\n    fn extract_failure_count(bead: &Bead) -> u32 {\n        bead.labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Sort candidates in deterministic priority order.\n    ///\n    /// Sort key: `(priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC)`.\n    /// The id tie-breaker ensures identical ordering across platforms.\n    fn sort_candidates(candidates: &mut [Bead]) {\n        candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            a.priority\n                .cmp(&b.priority)\n                .then_with(|| a.created_at.cmp(&b.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| a.id.as_ref().cmp(b.id.as_ref()))\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for PluckStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"pluck\"\n    }\n\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"strand.pluck\",\n        skip(self, store),\n        fields(\n            strand = \"pluck\",\n            exclude_labels = ?self.exclude_labels,\n        )\n    )]\n    async fn evaluate(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore) -> StrandResult {\n        // 1. Query bead store for ready, unassigned beads.\n        let filters = Filters {\n            assignee: None,\n            exclude_labels: self.exclude_labels.clone(),\n        };\n\n        let mut candidates = match store.ready(&filters).await {\n            Ok(beads) => beads,\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Bead store error is semantically different from NoWork.\n                return StrandResult::Error(StrandError::StoreError(e));\n            }\n        };\n\n        // 2. Filter: remove beads with excluded labels.\n        //    Defensive guard — store.ready() passes exclude_labels in its Filters,\n        //    but the backing CLI may not include label data in every query type.\n        //    Filtering here guarantees excluded-label beads are never presented as\n        //    candidates regardless of backend behaviour, preventing the\n        //    SELECTING→CLAIMING→RETRYING spin loop observed when br ready --json\n        //    omits label fields for some beads.\n        candidates.retain(|b| !b.labels.iter().any(|l| self.exclude_labels.contains(l)));\n\n        // 3. Filter: remove beads that are actively in_progress (claimed by another worker)\n        //    and Open beads with a stale assignee. These are never claimable — the claimer\n        //    will reject them every time, causing a hot loop.\n        candidates.retain(|b| {\n            !(matches!(b.status, crate::types::BeadStatus::InProgress)\n                || (b.status == crate::types::BeadStatus::Open && b.assignee.is_some()))\n        });\n\n        // 4. Sort: deterministic (priority, created_at, id).\n        Self::sort_candidates(&mut candidates);\n\n        // 5. Check for split trigger: if the first candidate has accumulated\n        //    enough consecutive failures, dispatch a SPLIT instruction instead\n        //    of returning the bead for normal processing.\n        if self.split_after_failures > 0 {\n            if let Some(first_candidate) = candidates.first() {\n                let failure_count = Self::extract_failure_count(first_candidate);\n                if failure_count >= self.split_after_failures {\n                    return StrandResult::Split(Box::new(first_candidate.clone()), failure_count);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 6. Return result.\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            StrandResult::NoWork\n        } else {\n            StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests The default labels are **not** merged with custom ones.\n\n### 3. Split Threshold (Auto-split Configuration)\n\n**Purpose**: Automatically trigger bead splitting when a bead accumulates too many consecutive failures\n\n**Default value**: `3` (beads are split after 3 consecutive failures)\n\n**How it works**:\n- Pluck extracts failure counts from bead labels following the pattern `failure-count:N`\n- When the first candidate bead's failure count >= threshold, Pluck returns a `Split` result instead of `BeadFound`\n- Threshold of `0` disables auto-split\n\n**Configuration methods**:\n```rust\n// Default threshold (3 failures)\nlet strand = PluckStrand::new(vec![]);\n\n// Custom threshold\nlet strand = PluckStrand::with_split_threshold(vec![], 5);\n\n// Disabled\nlet strand = PluckStrand::with_split_threshold(vec![], 0);\n```\n\n**Current configuration in ytt**: Using default threshold of 3\n\n### 4. Sorting Order (Deterministic Priority)\n\n**Hardcoded behavior** - not configurable\n\nPluck always sorts candidates in this order:\n1. **Priority** (ASC) - P0 before P1 before P2, etc.\n2. **Created at** (ASC) - Older beads first\n3. **Bead ID** (ASC) - Lexicographic tie-breaker for determinism\n\n**Why this matters**: Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same candidate list. This enables coordination without central server state.\n\n### 5. Additional Filters (Defensive Guards)\n\nThese filters are applied **after** the bead store query and are not configurable:\n\n**Filtered out**:\n- Beads with any excluded label (defensive guard against stores that don't apply label filtering)\n- Beads in `in_progress` status (claimed by another worker)\n- Open beads with a stale assignee (Open + assignee != None = not claimable)\n\n**Rationale**: These beads would cause the claimer to reject them every time, leading to a SELECTING→CLAIMING→RETRYING spin loop.\n\n## Current ytt Workspace Configuration\n\n### File: `.beads/config.yaml`\n\n```yaml\nissue_prefixes: [ytt]\ndefault_priority: 2\ndefault_type: task\nclaim_ttl_minutes: 30\n```\n\n### Pluck-Specific Settings\n\n**Exclude labels**: Using defaults (`deferred`, `human`, `blocked`, `starvation-alert`)\n\n**Split threshold**: Using default (3 failures)\n\n**Workspace path**: `/home/coding/ytt`\n\n**Bead store**: bead-forge SQLite backend at `.beads/beads.db`\n\n**CLI**: `~/.local/bin/br` (symlink to `bf` - bead-forge)\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\n### Normal Operation\n\n1. **Query**: Pluck calls `store.ready(filters)` with exclude_labels\n2. **Filter**: Defensive filtering removes excluded-label beads and unclaimable statuses\n3. **Sort**: Returns candidates sorted by priority, created_at, id\n4. **Split check**: If top bead has >=3 failure-count, returns Split result\n5. **Return**: `BeadFound(candidates)` or `NoWork` or `Split(bead, count)`\n\n### No Work Scenario\n\nPluck returns `NoWork` when:\n- All ready beads have excluded labels\n- No ready beads exist in the queue\n- Store returns empty list\n\n### Error Handling\n\nPluck returns `Error(StoreError)` when:\n- Bead store connection fails\n- Query execution fails\n- Data parsing errors occur\n\n## Integration with NEEDLE\n\n### Claiming Process (New with bead-forge)\n\n```bash\n# Old (race condition with 11+ workers)\nBEAD=$(br list --format json | jq -r '.[0].id')\nbr update $BEAD --status in_progress --assignee $WORKER\n\n# New (atomic, no race)\nbf claim --assignee $WORKER --format json\n```\n\nPluck's candidate list feeds directly into `bf claim`, which atomically claims the next available bead in a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction.\n\n### Strand Coordination\n\nPluck is the **primary strand** in NEEDLE's multi-strrand architecture:\n- **Pluck**: 90%+ of beads (normal work selection)\n- **Mend**: Retry beads with previous failures\n- **Other strands**: Specialized selection logic\n\n## Label Semantics\n\n### Standard Excluded Labels\n\n| Label | Purpose | When to apply |\n|-------|---------|---------------|\n| `deferred` | Beads intentionally delayed | Manual or automatic deferral |\n| `human` | Requires human intervention | Manual flag by user |\n| `blocked` | Blocked by dependencies | Automatic via dependency DAG |\n| `starvation-alert` | Starvation monitoring beads | NEEDLE auto-detection system |\n\n### Failure claimable)\n\n**Rationale**: These beads would cause the claimer to reject them every time, leading to a SELECTING→CLAIMING→RETRYING spin loop.\n\n## Current ytt Workspace Configuration\n\n### File: `.beads/config.yaml`\n\n```yaml\nissue_prefixes: [ytt]\ndefault_priority: 2\ndefault_type: task\nclaim_ttl_minutes: 30\n```\n\n### Pluck-Specific Settings\n\n**Exclude labels**: Using defaults (`deferred`, `human`, `blocked`, `starvation-alert`)\n\n**Split threshold**: Using default (3 failures)\n\n**Workspace path**: `/home/coding/ytt`\n\n**Bead store**: bead-forge SQLite backend at `.beads/beads.db`\n\n**CLI**: `~/.local/bin/br` (symlink to `bf` - bead-forge)\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\n### Normal Operation\n\n1. **Query**: Pluck calls `store.ready(filters)` with exclude_labels\n2. **Filter**: Defensive filtering removes excluded-label beads and unclaimable statuses\n3. **Sort**: Returns candidates sorted by priority, created_at, id\n4. **Split check**: If top bead has >=3 failure-count, returns Split result\n5. **Return**: `BeadFound(candidates)` or `NoWork` or `Split(bead, count)`\n\n### No Work Scenario\n\nPluck returns `NoWork` when:\n- All ready beads have excluded labels\n- No ready beads exist in the queue\n- Store returns empty list\n\n### Error Handling\n\nPluck returns `Error(StoreError)` when:\n- Bead store connection fails\n- Query execution fails\n- Data parsing errors occur\n\n## Integration with NEEDLE\n\n### Claiming Process (New with bead-forge)\n\n```bash\n# Old (race condition with 11+ workers)\nBEAD=$(br list --format json | jq -r '.[0].id')\nbr update $BEAD --status in_progress --assignee $WORKER\n\n# New (atomic, no race)\nbf claim --assignee $WORKER --format json\n```\n\nPluck's candidate list feeds directly into `bf claim`, which atomically claims the next available bead in a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction.\n\n### Strand Coordination\n\nPluck is the **primary strand** in NEEDLE's multi-strrand architecture:\n- **Pluck**: 90%+ of beads (normal work selection)\n- **Mend**: Retry beads with previous failures\n- **Other strands**: Specialized selection logic\n\n## Label Semantics\n\n### Standard Excluded Labels\n\n| Label | Purpose | When to apply |\n|-------|---------|---------------|\n| `deferred` | Beads intentionally delayed | Manual or automatic deferral |\n| `human` | Requires human intervention | Manual flag by user |\n| `blocked` | Blocked by dependencies | Automatic via dependency DAG |\n| `starvation-alert` | Starvation monitoring beads | NEEDLE auto-detection system |\n\n### Failure Count Labels\n\nPattern: `failure-count:N`\n\n- Applied by NEEDLE when a bead fails consecutive processing attempts\n- Read by Pluck to trigger auto-split at threshold (default: 3)\n- Example:
